beats.note: That is where the clock starts now. It is not where it started.

beats.name: UNIX Programmer's Manual, first edition
beats.role: Dated 3 November 1971. It counted time from 1 January 1971, not 1970.

beats.context: The first edition counted time in sixtieths of a second, as a 32 bit number.

beats.text: The manual admits it would run out.
beats.note: Its own BUGS section says 2**32 sixtieths of a second is only about 2.5 years.

beats.text: In 1973 the units became full seconds.
beats.note: Counted from the 1970 New Year. Wikipedia says engineers picked that date arbitrarily, as a convenient one.

beats.text: The zero point was a patch.
